newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AustVin valued at A$2.85 to A$3.13 a shr.
newsitem.headline: AustVin valued at A$2.85 to A$3.13 a shr.

text.p: Australian Vintage Ltd (AustVin) has released its Part B response to a takeover bid by Simeon Wines Ltd, formally recommending shareholders accept the offer and releasing an independent report valuing AustVin shares at between A$2.85 and A$3.13 a share.
The Simeon takeover for AustVin comprises two alternatives, which value AustVin shares at A$3.18 a share and A$3.12 a share respectively given Simeon's closing price of A$3.08 a share on Wednesday.
AustVin's shares closed unchanged at A$3.00 on Wednesday.
Simeon is offering four Simeon shares and A$3.60 cash for every five AustVin shares or one Simeon share and A$3.16 cash for every two AustVin shares.
The offers value AustVin at between A$115 million and A$117 million, given Simeon's A$3.08 closing share price on Wednesday.

"An independent expert, Price Waterhouse Corporate Finance Pty Ltd, has valued your AustVin Shares in the range of A$2.85 to A$3.13 and has concluded the offer is fair and reasonable," AustVin Chairman David Clarke said in the Part B response.
"In order to further improve the earnings power and quality of earnings of the company, we recommend acceptance of the Simeon offer," Clarke said.
Simeon said on June 27 when it made its second alternative offer that AustVin's directors would recommend the bid.

Simeon has said it would potentially need an extra A$32 million cash to fund the new alternative and would raise the funds through a share placement underwritten by Deutsche Morgan Grenfell of 10.6 million shares at A$3.05 a share.
The merged group would be Australia's fourth largest winemaker and would include two wine processing plants with an annual capacity of 100,000 tonnes processing 12 percent of Australia's grape crop.
In a substantial shareholder notice posted on Wednesday, Simeon said it was entitled to 2.6 million AustVin shares or 7.04 percent of its shares.
But AustVin's directors, who hold 25.5 percent of its shares, have said they intend to accept the offer.
